question.problem: Suppose that $|\,c\,|=12$, $|\,d\,|=6$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}.$ Find the vector projection of $d$ onto $c$ in terms of the vector $c.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{c}\,d & =|\,d\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =6\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $c:$

$$
u=\frac{c}{|\,c\,|}=\frac{c}{12}=\frac{1}{12}c
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{c}\,d & ={\text{comp}}_{c}\,d\cdot u \\  & =(-3)\cdot \frac{1}{12}c \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}c\end{aligned}
$$
